_source: Read off the panoramic video scoreboard (fixed camera, Rink 2 / SeatGeek sheet; board strip 430x115 at 3185,398, clock 64x36 at 3300,428). Periods 1 and 2 are stop time, so each goal is the moment the clock FROZE at the scoresheet value. Period 3 ran continuously -- the game was 2-10 by then -- so those times are read straight off the running clock, which is exact rather than approximate. Times are in the published master's timeline: master = panoramic - 53.73 (6.27s feed offset, minus the 60s cut point).
_offset_note: The 6.27s feed offset was NOT taken from the filenames, which imply the pano leads by 2s and have the SIGN backwards yet again (pano T225954 vs auto-follow T225956). Audio cross-correlation is normally the measurement, but both feeds on this camera are effectively silent (mean -67 dB, peak 104/32768, identical on both), so its peak/median was only 4.9x -- far below the usual STRONG threshold. Two things rescued it: envelope, high-frequency and variance features all returned the SAME -6.27s lag, and the scoreboard happens to be legible in the auto-follow feed itself around the 2nd-period 4:25 goal, where the clock ticks 4:31..4:25 and freezes at file2 t=591.5 against pano 2384 -- an offset bracket of 5.0-7.0s that contains 6.27 and excludes the filenames outright.
